fact_en: Swallow parents catch insects in flight, then carry them straight back to the nest to feed their hungry chicks.
fact_bis: Ang mga ginikanang sayaw magdala sa nadakpan nga insekto balik sa salag aron ipakaon sa ilang mga piso.

findings.note: title_bis 'Lunok ug Piso' — 'lunok' is the VERB to swallow/gulp, not the bird. The bird sense was mistranslated, so the title reads 'Gulping and Chicks'; the bird is never named in Cebuano in the title.

fact_en: Kapok fiber looks fluffy like cotton, but it's brittle and hard to spin — so unlike cotton, it's never woven into cloth.
fact_bis: Sama sa gapas ang tan-awon sa kapok, apan mabali kini ug lisod habihon — busa lahi sa gapas, dili gyud kini himoong panapton.

findings.note: title_bis 'Kapok Dili Bulak' — 'bulak' is flower; cotton is 'gapas' (used correctly in the body). The title asserts a different claim ('kapok is not a flower') than the card's point (kapok is not cotton).

fact_en: Worker ants dig and build the nest, making tunnels in soil or wood so the whole colony has a safe home.
fact_bis: Ang mga worker ant ang nagkalot ug nagtukod sa salag, naghimo og mga lungag sa yuta o kahoy aron adunay luwas nga puy-anan ang tibuok kolonya.

findings.note: title_bis 'Worker Langgam Hukay' — in Cebuano langgam = BIRD, not ant. The card is about worker ants digging nests (body keeps the English 'worker ant', so the title is the only Cebuano name for the animal and it names a different animal). Same class as the known cat-titled-iro defect. NOTE: this ant->langgam swap is corpus-wide (~40 cards in this sweep, many in the body text, e.g. ffct-01426 'Ang mga langgam nagbiya og...'), so the grep will hit broadly and legitimately.

fact_en:
Are all wasps fierce stingers?

Nope! Some wasps are tiny and can barely sting at all — instead, they help by eating pests that harm plants.
fact_bis:
Tanan ba nga putyukan peligroso?

Dili diay! Ang ubang matang sa putyukan gagmay kaayo ug halos dili makatukol — hinuon, motabang sila sa pagkaon sa peste sa tanom.

findings.note: English card is about WASPS (title_bis correctly says 'Tambuboan'), but the whole Cebuano body says 'putyukan' = honeybee: 'Tanan ba nga putyukan peligroso?... Ang ubang matang sa putyukan gagmay kaayo ug halos dili makatukol — hinuon, motabang sila sa pagkaon sa peste sa tanom.' A child reading only the Cebuano learns that some BEES barely sting and eat plant pests — a false claim about bees, and the wasp fact is never delivered. putyukan = bee throughout this corpus (e.g. the drone card ffct-11481); wasp is tamboboan/putakti.

fact_en:
When does a cicada grow wings?

Once it becomes an adult, ready to finally take flight.
fact_bis:
Kanus-a magkapako ang kagang?

Kon mahimo na kining hamtong ug andam na molupad.

findings.note: Wrong insect. EN is about a CICADA growing wings (title_bis correctly says 'Sikada'), but the body asks 'Kanus-a magkapako ang kagang?' — and corpus-wide 'kagang' is this corpus's word for CRICKET (8 other cards, all EN 'cricket': ffct-00655, ffct-01825, ffct-01874, ffct-03568, ffct-03598, ffct-03727, ffct-04846, ffct-11910); cicada is rendered 'kuliglig' elsewhere (ffct-11786 in this same batch). In general Cebuano 'kagang' is also a small crab, so a child reading only the body can learn that a crab/cricket is the animal that grows wings as an adult. The body never names the cicada, so the intended subject is not recoverable from the Cebuano text itself.

fact_en: Carbohydrates are the body's main source of energy. They break down into glucose for our cells, and any extra is stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles.
fact_bis: Ang carbohydrate mao ang panguna nga tinubdan sa enerhiya sa lawas. Napukan kini sa glucose nga gamiton sa mga selula, ug ang sobra gitipigan isip glycogen sa atay ug kaunuran.

findings.note: "Napukan kini sa glucose nga gamiton sa mga selula" — pukan/napukan is to fall or be felled (a tree, a person), not to break down/convert (matunaw, mabungkag, magub-a, which this corpus uses elsewhere). The card's mechanism step, carbohydrates BREAK DOWN INTO glucose, is destroyed; nothing else in the Cebuano restores it (title_bis is only "Carbohydrate Kusog"), so a Cebuano-only child gets carbs = energy and glycogen storage but never the carb->glucose conversion. Hapax: the only occurrence of napukan in the 47k-card sweep corpus.

fact_en:
How many times do we blink a day?

We blink about 15 to 20 times every minute, that adds up to around 28,000 blinks in one day!
fact_bis:
Pilay ka beses ta mokirok sa usa ka adlaw?

Mokirok kita og mga 15 hangtod 20 ka beses matag minuto, mokabat kini og gibana-bana nga 28,000 ka beses sa usa ka adlaw!

findings.note: Blink card. title_bis '28000 Sukmol Adlaw' — sukmol is a punch/blow, not a blink; and the body never rescues it because it uses 'mokirok' (a word that appears exactly once in 47k cards and not at all in the Cebuano CPT corpus) instead of the standard pilok/pamilok/kurap used by ~30 other blink cards. So the card only says we do some unnamed thing 15-20 times a minute, 28,000 times a day.

fact_en:
Why can you see a leaf's veins?

When a leaf rots, its soft parts vanish first, but the tougher veins last longer — that's why you sometimes see a lacy leaf skeleton.
fact_bis:
Nganong makita ang ugat sa tuyo nga dahon?

Kung malata ang dahon, ang humok nga bahin unang mawala, apan magpabilin ang gahi nga ugat — mao nga usahay makita nimo ang morag pukot nga bukog sa dahon.

findings.note: title_bis 'Gamot sa Uga nga Dahon' names leaf ROOTS (gamot) for leaf VEINS; the body correctly uses ugat, so the title heads a leaf-vein card with a plant part leaves do not have. Same title-level swap recurs at ffct-04299 ('Gamot Dahon Daloy') and ffct-06538 ('Gamot sa Dahon sa Bagyo'), while 19 other leaf-vein cards title it 'Ugat sa Dahon'.

fact_en:
How fast are your balance signals?

Signals zip incredibly fast from your ear to your brain through nerves, so your body can fix its balance almost instantly.
fact_bis:
Unsa kapaspas ang senyas sa balanse?

Paspas kaayo modagan ang senyas gikan sa dalunggan ngadto sa utok pinaagi sa mga nerbiyos, mao nga halos diha-diha maayo ang balanse.

findings.note: title_bis 'Paspas nga Signal sa Bali' — bali in Cebuano is a fracture/break (cf. ffct-02396 'First Aid sa Bali', ffct-02434 'Bali nga Bukog'), so the balance card is titled 'fast fracture signals'. Body correctly says balanse. Same truncation of balanse -> Bali also at ffct-01096 and ffct-01346.

fact_en: The Philippine crocodile is a small kind of crocodile — it usually grows only about three meters long!
fact_bis: Ang buaya nga Pilipino gamay nga matang sa buaya — kasagaran moabot lang og tulo ka metro ang gitas-on!

findings.note: Kapok seeds are said to be wrapped in 'humok nga puti nga BULAK' — bulak is flower in Cebuano (this is the Tagalog false friend bulak = cotton). The card never says fiber/lanot, so a Cebuano-only child reads that kapok seeds are wrapped in soft white flowers and that flowers are stuffed into pillows. Every other kapok card in the corpus uses lanot / hibla / lugas / balhibo; the CPT Cebuano corpus uses bulak exclusively for flower and gapas for cotton.

fact_en: In the rainforest, bats, birds, and bees pollinate flowers and spread seeds when they eat fruit — helping trees keep growing and spreading!
fact_bis: Sa rainforest, ang mga kabog, langgam, ug putyukan motabang sa pagpamulak sa bulak ug pagsabwag sa liso kung mokaon sila og prutas — mao nga nagpadayon ang pagdaghan sa mga kahoy!

findings.note: English 'bats, birds, and bees pollinate flowers and spread seeds' becomes 'motabang sa pagpamulak sa bulak' = help the flowers BLOOM. Pollination is replaced by a different process and nothing in the card restores it (no polen/polinasyon), so the child learns that fruit-eating animals make flowers bloom. 26+ corpus cards use polinasyon/pollinate; the one other card that uses pagpamulak (ffct-07113) repairs it with 'pinaagi sa pagdala sa polen'.

fact_en:
Why is it called 'formic acid'?

Some ants, like wood ants, spray formic acid to defend themselves — 'formic' comes from the Latin word 'formica,' meaning ant!
fact_bis:
Nganong 'formic acid' ang tawag niini?

Ang pipila ka langgam sama sa wood ants nagaspray og formic acid isip depensa — gikan kini sa Latin nga 'formica' nga nagpasabot og langgam!

findings.note: Formic acid card: Cebuano body renders 'ants' as 'langgam', which is BIRD in Cebuano (Tagalog false friend). Reads 'Ang pipila ka langgam sama sa wood ants nagaspray og formic acid' and, fatally, 'gikan kini sa Latin nga formica nga nagpasabot og langgam' — so the card's entire point teaches that formica means bird. Never corrected in the body; only title_bis ('Hulmigas ug Asido') has the right word.
